Find the least and most typical sequences

Source: R/mine.R
mine_sequences.Rd

mine_sequences() ranks sequences by how well a fitted tree predicts them and returns the top n. With which = "surprising", the sequences with the highest perplexity come first: those whose transitions the tree finds least expected, which are candidates for atypical cases or for patterns that the fitting data did not contain. With which = "expected", the sequences with the lowest perplexity come first: the most typical sequences under the tree.

The ranking is by per-sequence perplexity from score_sequences(), which adjusts for sequence length. When newdata are the fitting sequences themselves, the ranking describes typicality within the data; with other sequences it describes how well the tree generalizes to them. To find where within a sequence the unexpected moves occur, use score_positions().

Usage

mine_sequences(tree, newdata, n = 10L, which = c("surprising", "expected"))

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

newdata

Sequences to rank, in any form accepted by context_tree().

n

Number of sequences to return. Default 10.

which

"surprising" (default; highest perplexity first) or "expected" (lowest perplexity first).

Value

A data.frame with the columns of score_sequences() (sequence_id, n_scored, log_lik, perplexity), one row per sequence, at most n rows.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree or newdata has no usable sequence.

See also

score_sequences(), score_positions(), mine_contexts().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 2)
mine_sequences(tree, engagement, n = 5)
#>   sequence_id n_scored   log_lik perplexity
#> 1         230       23 -30.83375   3.821328
#> 2         126       24 -31.93443   3.783317
#> 3         552       25 -32.46789   3.664587
#> 4         775       25 -32.35544   3.648140
#> 5         129       23 -28.75226   3.490686
mine_sequences(tree, engagement, n = 5, which = "expected")
#>   sequence_id n_scored  log_lik perplexity
#> 1         354       25 -6.89971   1.317833
#> 2         365       25 -6.89971   1.317833
#> 3         450       25 -6.89971   1.317833
#> 4         536       25 -6.89971   1.317833
#> 5         539       25 -6.89971   1.317833
